subject: Bounded runtime topology — control plane/data plane review

Subject: Bounded runtime topology — control plane/data plane review

Hi Olga / EdgeCore team,

Thanks again for hosting the workshop last week. Attached is a first-pass reference diagram for the private runtime topology we discussed — the goal is to lock down the control-plane <-> data-plane boundaries, egress constraints, and required network primitives before we hand this over to infra for provisioning.

Key things I want feedback on from EdgeCore and our infra leads (Irene, Jonas):
- Control plane endpoints: which endpoints must be reachable from customer VPC vs. kept in the private control plane (auth, model registry, rollout API)?
- Data plane NAT/egress: recommended pattern for egress proofing and minimal IP ranges (NAT gateway, proxy sidecar, or forced-tunnel to central egress)?
- Cross-subnet latency: expected RTT sensitivity for KV-cache warm paths and batching — any recommended colocations?
- BGP / peering implications if customer wants BGP-based route advertisement for peered private deployments.

I've attached a drawio export (20250907-runtime-topology-v1.drawio.png) and a control/data matrix spreadsheet that maps services to network zones (control-data-matrix.xlsx). Please review and call out anything missing.

Next step: propose a short sync (30m) Wed morning to finalize.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 8 Sep 2025 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bounded runtime topology — control plane/data plane review

Rishi,

Thanks — the diagrams are a good starting point. High level comments from EdgeCore:

1) Control plane placement: keep auth (OIDC/JWK), model registry, and rollout coordinator inside the customer-managed control plane VPC where possible. That minimizes trust boundaries and avoids cross-tenant metadata leakage. Exposed public endpoints should be limited to a single egress-protected gateway (we call it the control-origination-proxy).

2) Data plane egress: recommend forced-tunnel model to a hardened egress proxy in the customer environment. Avoid NAT-ing inference nodes directly to the Internet. This also makes data egress auditing easier.

3) Latency/colocation: for KV cache hot-paths, colocate cache nodes with inference nodes in the same subnet/AZ. If customers span multiple AZs, use read-replicas in each AZ to reduce cross-AZ hop counts.

4) BGP/peering: BGP is fine but keep route adverts limited to the block used for inference-pool subnets to prevent accidental route leakage. Use BGP communities to tag inference vs control prefixes.

We have a couple of follow-ups:
- Can you enumerate which control plane APIs will require TLS client certs vs token-based auth?
- On the matrix sheet, column "Acceptable egress pattern" needs explicit examples per service.

Happy to jump on Wed — propose 09:30 PT.

Best,
Olga
Lead Solutions Architect
EdgeCore Systems

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 9 Sep 2025 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bounded runtime topology — control plane/data plane review

Thanks for the draft, Rishi — good call capturing the service-to-zone mapping. A few internal notes and requests before the sync:

- Auth and telemetry: We should treat telemetry ingestion (metrics/traces) as control-plane-adjacent: customers may want those to be pushed to their SIEM. Add a telemetry egress row in the spreadsheet (syslog/OTLP endpoints).

- mTLS for control-plane internal APIs: we prefer mutual TLS between our control-plane components and customer's ops endpoints for high-trust tenants. Token-only flows are ok for lower-tier hosted endpoints. Please mark the APIs that must enforce mTLS in the matrix.

- Network ACLs/CIDRs: propose using a three-block CIDR allocation per customer: 1) control-plane management / API, 2) inference/data-plane, 3) infra-services (cache, metrics, proxies). Keeps ACLs simpler for onprem customers that require explicit firewall rules.

- Operational note: we need to spell out upgrade path for the KV cache schema and how we migrate cache replicas across AZs — include a short bullet in the drawio or an appendix on migration handshake expectations.

I can prepare a short runbook excerpt for the sync. Wed 09:30 PT works for me.

Irene
Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@edgecore.io>
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 16:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bounded runtime topology — control plane/data plane review

Following up after today's sync — notes and agreed actions (summary):

1) Finalized boundary: Control plane = model registry, rollout API, auth/token service, telemetry bridge. Data plane = inference nodes, KV cache, local proxies. Control plane services will be reachable only over a customer-managed peering or via the control-origination-proxy with strict egress ACLs.

2) Egress approach: Forced-tunnel to customer egress proxy is the default for private/onprem. For customers that cannot provide a central egress, we will document a hardened NAT pattern with extra auditing hooks (Flow logs + sidecar forwarding).

3) Security modes: Two modes will be documented — "High-trust" (mTLS + cert rotation + out-of-band telemetry delivery) and "Standard" (token-based auth, aggregated telemetry). We will add a matrix mapping tenant tiers to required controls in control-data-matrix.xlsx.

4) Network plan: Jonas to provide recommended CIDR block sizes and sample iptables / network ACL snippets for infra teams. Kimberly to add a short section in the runbook on KV cache migration and risk windows. Rishi to push an updated diagram with callouts for the egress proxy and BGP community recommendations.

Next steps and deadlines:
- Jonas: CIDR + ACL sample (due 2025-09-14)
- Kimberly: KV migration appendix (due 2025-09-14)
- Rishi: Updated diagram and matrix (due 2025-09-15)

Thanks all — this aligns us for the handoff to infra on 2025-09-17.

Jonas Weber
Infrastructure Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
